reports.text: Noncontrast CT of the head. No intracranial hemorrhage, mass or mass effect. Ventricles and sulci are normal in size for age; no hydrocephalus. Gray-white differentiation preserved. Basal cisterns are patent. Visualized paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are clear.

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN NOTE - regional hospital
Date of service: 01/05/2026

CC: headache, fever, stiff neck, confusion

HPI: 31-year-old man with paranoid schizophrenia and latent TB infection, which has gone essentially untreated because he took his isoniazid so irregularly. Brought by his parents. For two weeks he has had a severe headache, fevers and a stiff neck. Over the last few days he has become muddled and increasingly sleepy, per his parents.

PMH: paranoid schizophrenia with nonadherence; latent TB (positive IGRA 2022); prior antipsychotic dystonic reactions; falciparum malaria 5/2025, treated.
Meds: risperidone 4 mg BID, aripiprazole 10 mg daily, isoniazid 300 mg daily (adherence poor).
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: T 38.5 C, BP 126/80, HR 98, RR 18, SpO2 98% RA.
Drowsy but rousable, confused to date and place. Nuchal rigidity. Brudzinski sign positive. Right abducens nerve palsy: right eye does not abduct past midline. Pupils equal and reactive. Other cranial nerves intact. Moves all limbs symmetrically. Lungs clear. Heart regular. No rash.

Studies:
- CT head without contrast before lumbar puncture: no mass, bleeding or hydrocephalus.
- Lumbar puncture. CSF: WBC 150/uL (lymphocytes 80%), RBC 10/uL, protein 100 mg/dL, glucose 30 mg/dL against a serum glucose of 90; ADA 12 U/L, elevated. CSF sent for AFB culture.
- CBC and BMP normal.

Impression: subacute lymphocytic meningitis with low CSF glucose, high protein and elevated ADA, in a patient with untreated latent TB and a right sixth nerve palsy: tuberculous meningitis.
Plan: infectious disease consulted from the ED. Admit to medicine for four-drug TB therapy with adjunctive dexamethasone and further imaging.

reports.conclusion: No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality. No radiographic evidence of pulmonary tuberculosis.

documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
HOSPITAL MEDICINE - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 01/05/2026. Discharged: 01/23/2026.
Infectious disease consulting.

Principal diagnosis: tuberculous meningitis, in the setting of untreated latent TB infection.
Secondary: right abducens (sixth nerve) palsy; paranoid schizophrenia.

Workup:
- CT head (pre-LP): no mass or hydrocephalus.
- CSF as per ED record: lymphocytic pleocytosis, protein 100, glucose 30 (serum 90), ADA 12. CSF AFB culture sent 01/05 and still pending at discharge.
- MRI brain with and without contrast: enhancement of the basal meninges; no hydrocephalus; no infarct.
- Chest x-ray: clear.
- HIV antigen/antibody, hepatitis B surface antigen and hepatitis C antibody: all negative.
- Hepatic panel 01/06 normal (AST 24, ALT 16).
- Weight 70 kg.

Course: started isoniazid 300 mg, rifampin 600 mg, pyrazinamide 1500 mg and ethambutol 1200 mg daily with pyridoxine 50 mg daily, and dexamethasone IV, changed to an oral taper as he improved. Fever resolved over the first week. Headache eased and his confusion cleared gradually. The right sixth nerve palsy is improving but still present at discharge. Psychiatric medications continued; he was calm on the ward.

Treatment plan (per ID):
- Intensive phase: isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide, ethambutol and pyridoxine daily for two months, to early March 2026.
- Dexamethasone oral taper per the schedule given, to stop at eight weeks (early March 2026).
- Continuation phase: isoniazid, rifampin and pyridoxine for ten further months, planned end early January 2027.
- Case reported to the local public health department. Medications to be given by directly observed therapy (DOT) through public health, starting the day after discharge.
- Outpatient infectious disease clinic monthly.
- Monthly LFTs and monthly visual acuity and color vision checks while on ethambutol; PCP office has agreed to do these.

Drug interaction: rifampin lowers blood levels of risperidone and aripiprazole. Psychiatry is asked to watch for relapse. No antipsychotic dose change made.

Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge medications:
- isoniazid 300 mg daily (DOT)
- rifampin 600 mg daily (DOT)
- pyrazinamide 1500 mg daily (DOT)
- ethambutol 1200 mg daily (DOT)
- pyridoxine 50 mg daily
- dexamethasone oral taper, per schedule
- risperidone 4 mg twice daily
- aripiprazole 10 mg daily

Disposition: home with parents. PCP visit within one week; ID clinic in about a month.

documents.title: Post-discharge visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Transitional care visit after admission 1/5-1/23 for tuberculous meningitis. Here with both parents. Discharge summary and 1/26 ID letter reviewed.

Hospital course in brief: two weeks of headache, fever and neck stiffness, then confusion and drowsiness. LP: lymphocytic CSF, low glucose, high protein, elevated ADA. MRI with basal meningeal enhancement, no hydrocephalus. Chest x-ray clear. HIV, hepatitis B and C negative. Started four-drug TB therapy with pyridoxine and dexamethasone. Reported to public health; DOT started after discharge. CSF AFB culture reported 1/26: M. tuberculosis complex, susceptibilities pending.

Today: headache gone. Confusion gone per parents; he is back to his usual self. No fever. Eating. Takes DOT doses each morning with the public health nurse.
Psych: on risperidone 4 mg BID and aripiprazole 10 mg daily, unchanged. No change in voices or behavior noted by family so far.

Meds reconciled: isoniazid 300 mg, rifampin 600 mg, pyrazinamide 1500 mg, ethambutol 1200 mg daily (DOT); pyridoxine 50 mg daily; dexamethasone oral taper per hospital schedule; risperidone 4 mg BID; aripiprazole 10 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

BP 118/73, HR 71, RR 17, T 36.7, SpO2 98%, Wt 69.2 kg, BMI 22.5.
Alert, oriented x3, answers appropriately in his usual brief way. Neck supple. Right eye: abduction limited but better than described at discharge; other eye movements full. Pupils equal and reactive. Remaining cranial nerves intact. Strength and gait normal. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, no hepatomegaly. Sclerae anicteric.
Vision (ethambutol monitoring): Snellen 20/20 right, 20/20 left. Ishihara plates all read correctly each eye.

A/P:
1. Tuberculous meningitis, culture-confirmed, on intensive phase via DOT. Clinically much improved. Hepatic panel today and monthly. Monthly vision checks while on ethambutol. Problem list updated: latent TB replaced by tuberculous meningitis.
2. Right sixth nerve palsy, improving.
3. Paranoid schizophrenia: called psychiatry office re the rifampin interaction flagged in the discharge summary. They have the summary and will see him in February; no dose change for now.
RTC 4 weeks.
